source_text:
ταύτῃ τοι καὶ οὐ διέλαθεν αὐτὴν οὕτω καθεύδουσαν ἡ φωνὴ τοῦ νυμφίου· καὶ γὰρ
τὴν θύραν κρούοντος ἤσθετο καὶ εἶπεν· φωνὴ ἀδελφιδοῦ μου κρούει ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν.
1 Thess 5,9 Ὅτι οὐκ ἐν τοῖς κατακρινομένοις, ἀλλ' ἐν τοῖς σωζομένοις. 1 Thess 5,10
∆ιὰ τοῦτό φησιν· ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἀπέθανεν ὁ Χριστός, ἵνα εἴτε γρηγορῶμεν, τοῦτ' ἔστι
ζῶμεν, εἴτε καθεύδωμεν, τοῦτ' ἔστιν εἴτε ἀποθάνωμεν–ἄλλως γὰρ ὧδε τὸ καθεύδειν
καὶ οὐχ ὡς ἄνω ἐξέλαβεν–ἅμα σὺν αὐτῷ ζήσωμεν. οἱ γὰρ τὰ εἰρημένα ὅπλα
κτησάμενοι συζήσουσι καὶ συμβασιλεύσουσι Χριστῷ. 1 Thess 5,19®21 Τότε σβέννυται
τὸ πνεῦμα, ὅταν ἡ πολιτεία ἀναξία ᾖ τῆς πίστεως. Προφητείας μὴ ἐξουθενεῖτε. πάντα
δοκιμάζετε. μήτε, φησίν, ἐνεδρεύητε τοῦ πνεύματος τὰς ἀποκρύψεις, μήτε πᾶσαν
ἀπαγγελίαν ἀδοκιμάστως παραδέχεσθε. 1 Thess 5,23 Οὐδαμοῦ ἐπ' ἀπίστου τὰ τρία
τέθεικε, πνεῦμα ψυχὴ σῶμα, ἀλλ' ἐπὶ μόνων τῶν πιστευόντων, ὧν ψυχὴ μὲν καὶ
σῶμα τῆς φύσεως, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα τῆς εὐεργεσίας, τοῦτ' ἔστι τὸ χάρισμα τῶν
πιστευόντων. καὶ οὐκ εἶπεν «ἄμεμπτα» τηρηθείη, ἵνα μὴ νομίσῃς ὅτι ὑπὲρ τῶν
χαρισμάτων εὔχεται, ἀλλ' ἀμέμπτως, τοῦτ' ἔστιν ἡμῶν ἀμέμπτως διαγόντων καὶ
διατηρούντων διὰ τῆς εὐσεβείας.
thought_title: The bride hears the bridegroom; Paul on living with Christ, testing prophecy, and blamelessness
orientation: Severianus is closing his comments on 1 Thessalonians, first finishing the bride's words from Song of Songs, then explaining Paul's statements about salvation, death, the Spirit, prophecy, and the threefold blessing on believers.
pass_a_gloss: For this reason indeed the voice of the bridegroom did not escape her notice as she was sleeping in this way; for she perceived him knocking at the door and said: The voice of my beloved knocks at the door. Because not among those who are condemned, but among those who are saved. For this reason he says: Christ died for us, so that whether we are awake, that is, we live, or whether we sleep, that is, whether we die—for here he took sleeping differently and not as above—we may live together with him. For those who have acquired the weapons that were spoken of will live together with Christ and will reign together with Christ. Then the spirit is quenched, when the way of life is unworthy of the faith. Do not despise prophecies. Test all things. Neither, he says, should you lie in wait for the hidden things of the spirit, nor should you accept every report without testing. Nowhere has he placed the three things, spirit, soul, body, upon an unbeliever, but upon believers only, whose soul and body are of nature, but the spirit is of the benefaction, that is, the gift of believers. And he did not say may they be kept blameless, so that you might not think that he is praying on behalf of the gifts, but blamelessly, that is, while we conduct ourselves blamelessly and keep them through piety.

choices.why: The Song of Songs term for the bridegroom; rendered as a noun of endearment rather than literally 'brother's son' or 'kinsman,' which would misrepresent the nuptial context.
Kept as the literal verb for sleep to preserve the contrast Paul draws between literal death and the earlier figurative sleep of the bride; the gloss marks the shift in sense.

choices.english: the weapons that were spoken of
choices.why: Refers back to the armor imagery earlier in the commentary; rendered literally to keep the anaphoric force.
In this ethical context it means conduct or manner of living, not civic government; the rendering keeps the moral sense.
Refers to prophetic utterances or messages being delivered; 'report' keeps the neutral sense of a spoken announcement that must be tested.
The adverb is deliberately contrasted with the adjective 'blameless'; rendering it as an adverb preserves Severianus's point that Paul prays for blameless conduct, not blameless gifts.

bible_refs.note: φωνὴ ἀδελφιδοῦ μου κρούει ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν
Ὅτι οὐκ ἐν τοῖς κατακρινομένοις, ἀλλ' ἐν τοῖς σωζομένοις
ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἀπέθανεν ὁ Χριστός, ἵνα εἴτε γρηγορῶμεν εἴτε καθεύδωμεν ἅμα σὺν αὐτῷ ζήσωμεν

pass_b_english: So the bridegroom's voice did not escape her notice while she slept in this way. She heard him knocking at the door and said: "The voice of my beloved is knocking at the door" (Song of Songs 5:2).

"Because God has not destined us for wrath, but for obtaining salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ" (1 Thessalonians 5:9). For this reason Paul says: "Christ died for us, so that whether we are awake—that is, alive—or asleep—that is, whether we die, for here he takes sleeping in a different sense than above—we may live together with him" (1 Thessalonians 5:10). For those who have acquired the weapons that were spoken of will live together with Christ and reign together with Christ.

The spirit is quenched whenever the way of life is unworthy of the faith. "Do not despise prophecies. Test everything" (1 Thessalonians 5:19-21). Do not, Paul says, lie in wait for the hidden things of the spirit, nor accept every report without testing it either.

Nowhere has Paul placed the three—spirit, soul, body—upon an unbeliever, but only upon those who believe. Their soul and body belong to nature, but the spirit belongs to God's kindness—that is, the gift of those who believe. And he did not say "may they be kept blameless," so that you would not think he is praying for the gifts, but "blamelessly"—that is, with us conducting ourselves blamelessly and preserving them through godliness.

problems.quote: but do not accept every report without testing it either
problems.why: The Greek has no 'but'—μήτε...μήτε is 'neither...nor.' Adding 'but' changes the construction to a false contrast.
problems.fix: nor accept every report without testing it either

problems.quote: may we conduct ourselves blamelessly and preserve them through godliness
problems.source_quote: ἡμῶν ἀμέμπτως διαγόντων καὶ διατηρούντων διὰ τῆς εὐσεβείας
problems.why: The participles are genitive absolute/causal, not hortatory 'may we'; Severianus explains the meaning of 'blamelessly,' not exhorting.
problems.fix: with us conducting ourselves blamelessly and preserving them through godliness
problems.ruling: Genitive participles ἡμῶν διαγόντων καὶ διατηρούντων are causal/explanatory, not hortatory; 'may we' misreads the grammar.

edits.old: but do not accept every report without testing it either
edits.new: nor accept every report without testing it either

edits.old: may we conduct ourselves blamelessly and preserve them through godliness
edits.new: with us conducting ourselves blamelessly and preserving them through godliness

fixed: Changed 'but do not accept' to 'nor accept' to match μήτε...μήτε (neither...nor).
Changed 'may we conduct' to 'with us conducting' to reflect the genitive absolute/causal participles explaining 'blamelessly.'

last_rejected.quote: live together with Christ and reign together with Christ
last_rejected.why: Source has 'with him' (αὐτῷ), not 'with Christ' twice; second 'Christ' is dative but first refers back to Christ already mentioned.
last_rejected.fix: will live together with him and reign together with Christ.
last_rejected.ruling: Χριστῷ is dative after both verbs; 'with Christ' twice is valid. αὐτῷ in prior clause refers to Christ.

last_rejected.why: ἐνεδρεύω means 'lie in ambush for, waylay,' but context demands 'spy on' or 'pry into' hidden things; 'lie in wait' suggests physical ambush, wrong sense here.
last_rejected.fix: Do not, Paul says, pry into the hidden things of the spirit.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐνεδρεύω means 'lie in wait for/ambush'; 'lie in wait for hidden things' conveys prying adequately here.

last_rejected.why: εὐεργεσία means 'benefaction, good deed, bounty,' not abstract 'kindness'; this is the spirit as God's gift/benefaction to believers.
last_rejected.fix: but the spirit belongs to benefaction—that is, the gift of those who believe.
last_rejected.ruling: εὐεργεσία = benefaction/kindness; 'God's kindness' is within range and glossed as 'gift' next clause.
